questions.explanation: TCP estimates the round-trip time and sets a timer with some margin above it. If an acknowledgement for outstanding data does not arrive before the timer expires, the sender assumes loss and retransmits. A timeout is a recovery action, not a closure; too short a value causes needless retries while too long a value wastes time after a real loss. The concrete addresses in the case do not change the rule.
